Methodology Note: This project builds a quantitative 2026 World Cup pricing model that estimates fair probabilities for match outcomes and compares them against Kalshi market-implied probabilities.
The objective is not simply to pick winners, but to identify potential mispriced outcomes where model probability exceeds market probability.
The project is framed as a finance/econ-style market-pricing model using sports event contracts as the tradable asset.
model_pick identifies the most likely match outcome. best_value identifies the outcome with the highest model-versus-market edge. These can differ.
Moneyline production model is v0.2 (frozen). O/U production model is v0.3 (situational + multiplicative scalars).
v0.2 moneyline is the clean base model using team-quality differentials only.
v0.3 moneyline overlay is experimental and not used for live signals.
v0.3 O/U was promoted to production because goal totals are more sensitive to situational context (climate/venue/tactical) than binary match outcomes.
v0.2 O/U is preserved in ou_model_vo2_FROZEN for forward-test comparison against v0.3 O/U.
Official dashboard outputs: model_output for moneyline (from v0.2), ou_model for O/U (from v0.3).
v0.2 moneyline uses team-strength differential, last-5 goal differential, xG differential, and last-5 form.
Team-strength differential is sourced from Opta Power Ratings; the column is labeled 'elo' for historical reasons but contains Opta data.
The original Opta-vs-Elo dual-anchor design was collapsed to a single quality measure to avoid double-counting.
Shots on target was not included in v0.2 raw_score because it overlaps with xG and goal differential. May be added after calibration.
Climate, altitude, host status, venue tier, and tactical style were collected but excluded from official v0.2 moneyline output.
Climate, altitude, venue tier, and tactical style ARE used in v0.3 O/U production.
Positive matchup-difference values indicate an advantage for the listed home team. In this project, home_team means listed team, not true home-field advantage.
raw_score = (elo_diff*0.06) + (gd_last5_diff*0.15) + (xg_diff_diff*0.35) + (form_diff*0.08).
home_strength = 1 / (1 + EXP(-raw_score)).
home_strength represents the listed home team's share of non-draw win probability.
draw_prob is estimated separately using matchup closeness rather than being derived directly from the home/away sigmoid split.
draw_prob formula: MAX(0.18, MIN(0.35, 0.30 - ABS(elo_diff) * 0.003)). Base 30%, reduced by 0.3pp per Opta gap, floored at 18%, capped at 35%.
home_win_prob = (1 - draw_prob) * home_strength.
away_win_prob = (1 - draw_prob) * (1 - home_strength).
home_win_prob + draw_prob + away_win_prob should always sum to 100%.
A systematic issue was identified where the model over-flagged draws as STRONG PLAYs in heavy-favorite matches.
This occurred because the draw probability floor was too high relative to market prices in severe mismatch games.
Examples of suspicious draw edges include heavy favorites such as Germany, Spain, Brazil, France, or Portugal where market draw probability is extremely low.
A draw can still be legitimate value in balanced matchups, but heavy-favorite draws require additional review before action.
draw_play_filter flags suspicious draw value when best_value = Draw, market_draw is very low, and raw_score indicates a large mismatch.
Current draw block logic: BLOCK DRAW when best_value = Draw, market_draw < 15%, and ABS(raw_score) > 1.5.
Blocked draw rows are converted to REVIEW instead of STRONG PLAY / PLAY.
The draw_play_filter does not change probabilities. It only changes signal classification to prevent blindly acting on likely model artifacts.
The draw engine is a known candidate for future calibration using historical match data and/or Poisson scoreline probabilities.
Opta Power Ratings is used as the primary team-strength measure (stored in team_stats column labeled 'elo' for historical reasons).
xG inputs are compiled from regional qualifier and tournament data (UEFA, CONMEBOL, CAF, AFC, CONCACAF, Gold Cup).
Goal differential and form are based on recent competitive results (Kaggle martj42 international results 1872-present).
Friendlies are excluded from core competitive form calculations where possible.
Some pre-WC friendly-style competitions (FIFA Series, Kirin Cup, King's Cup) occasionally bypass the friendly filter.
Some regional xG datasets are less complete than others, creating a known comparability limitation (partially mitigated by conf_scalar in O/U).
New Zealand has no available xG source and uses a goals-based fallback.
team_stats is the master team-level database.
model_inputs_v02 pulls team-level statistics from team_stats and converts them into matchup-level difference features.
ou_model pulls team-level statistics from team_stats with conf_scalar adjustment applied at the input level.
Historical teams not participating in the 2026 World Cup are not forced into team_stats.
Raw historical competition tabs are kept separate from the current 2026 prediction dataset.
Team naming is standardized across tabs to avoid lookup errors. Examples: USA, IR Iran, Czechia, Cabo Verde, Côte d'Ivoire, DR Congo, Turkey.
Kalshi is used as the primary market benchmark; Polymarket is a secondary reference.
Raw Kalshi home/draw/away prices are normalized so the three-outcome market sums to 100%.
market_home = kalshi_home_raw / (kalshi_home_raw + kalshi_draw_raw + kalshi_away_raw).
The same normalization logic is applied to market_draw and market_away.
The same proportional devig is applied separately to O/U contracts (over_raw and under_raw).
Market probabilities should be updated close to kickoff because prices can move materially before the match.
edge_home = model_home_prob - market_home.
edge_draw = model_draw_prob - market_draw.
edge_away = model_away_prob - market_away.
best_edge is the largest edge among home, draw, and away.
best_value is the outcome with the highest model-versus-market edge.
best_value can differ from model_pick because the most likely outcome is not always the best-priced outcome.
A positive edge means the model prices the outcome higher than the market. A negative edge means the model prices it lower than the market.
Same logic applies to O/U: ou_best_value is over or under whichever has the larger devigged edge; ou_best_edge tracks magnitude.
STRONG PLAY: best_edge >= 10%, unless blocked by review logic.
PLAY: best_edge >= 6%, unless blocked by review logic.
WATCH: best_edge >= 3%.
PASS: best_edge < 3%.
Any best_edge >= 15% is flagged CHECK INPUTS for manual review.
CHECK INPUTS does not automatically mean the play is invalid; it means the odds and team inputs should be verified before action.
REVIEW is used when a row is either CHECK INPUTS or BLOCK DRAW.
REVIEW rows should not be treated as automatic plays. They require manual verification before being considered actionable.
Signal hierarchy: REVIEW override fires first, then STRONG PLAY, PLAY, WATCH, PASS.
Same thresholds apply to O/U signals via ou_signal column.
review_flag = CHECK INPUTS when best_edge >= 15%.
draw_play_filter = BLOCK DRAW when best_value = Draw, market_draw < 15%, and ABS(raw_score) > 1.5.
signal = REVIEW when review_flag = CHECK INPUTS or draw_play_filter = BLOCK DRAW.
This prevents the model from automatically firing on extreme edges that may result from stale odds, bad inputs, or draw-probability artifacts.
Large edges are not removed from the dashboard; they are preserved but marked for review to maintain transparency.

weak_schedule_flag (per team in team_stats) = 1 if team's xG source is from a materially weaker confederation pool (AFC qualifiers / CAF qualifiers / CONCACAF non-host qualifiers / OFC fallback); 0 otherwise.
weak_schedule_match = FLAG when home_team.weak_schedule_flag != away_team.weak_schedule_flag (XOR logic). Fires only on cross-pool matchups, not same-pool.
The flag does not modify probabilities. It surfaces matches where the unadjusted xg_diff_diff may be distorted by pool baseline differences.
Moneyline-specific. The O/U model handles confederation comparability directly at the input level via conf_scalar. Moneyline does not apply conf_scalar to avoid double-counting with F1 Opta.
Bucketing live results by weak_schedule_match indicates whether moneyline systematically over- or under-predicts on cross-pool matches, informing v1.1 calibration.
conf_scalar is a per-team multiplier in team_stats column L, derived from average Elo per confederation.
Values: UEFA 1.00 (baseline), CAF 0.96, CONMEBOL 0.88, AFC 0.87, CONCACAF Gold Cup 0.87, OFC 0.80.
conf_scalar is ACTIVE in O/U production. Applied to xG inputs at the input level (before per-team scalars and match-level situational modifier).
Offensive xG adjustment is multiplicative discount: xg_for_adj = xg_for * conf_scalar.
Defensive xG adjustment is elo-weighted blend: xg_against_adj = (xg_against/conf_scalar)*(elo/100) + xg_against*(1-elo/100).
Defensive xG is inflated (divided by scalar) rather than discounted because weak-pool defenses understate true leakiness against UEFA-level attack.
Elo weighting in defensive xG acts as empirical-Bayes shrinkage: stronger teams get more confederation adjustment, weaker teams stay closer to raw.
conf_scalar is NOT applied to moneyline. F1 Opta differential already encodes confederation strength, so multiplying xG by conf_scalar would double-count.
The CONMEBOL value (0.88) is a known calibration concern. Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay rate higher than 0.88 implies; the average may be skewed by weaker CONMEBOL nations.
Coefficients are uncalibrated against forward-test data; values will be re-derived from observed CLV by confederation post-tournament.
v0.3 moneyline overlay adds climate, altitude, venue tier, host status, tactical primary style, and tactical secondary style as a research extension.
v0.3 moneyline overlay is tracked side-by-side with v0.2 frozen moneyline; NOT used for live signals.
v0.3 moneyline weights are uncalibrated and could produce aggressive edge signals if promoted prematurely.
When v0.3 moneyline is promoted in v1.1+, situational_score will be capped: MAX(-0.75, MIN(0.75, situational_score)).
O/U production lives in ou_model tab (v0.3 architecture). v0.2 O/U archived in ou_model_vo2_FROZEN.
O/U inputs use asymmetric confederation adjustment: xg_for is discounted (multiply by conf_scalar), xg_against is elo-weighted blend of inflated and raw.
Per-team expected goals use 60/40 weighting: home_exp_goals = (home_xg_for_adj * 0.6) + (away_xg_against_adj * 0.4).
60/40 split reflects that attacking output is more stable across opponents than defensive output is across attackers.
Per-team adj_xg applies multiplicative tactical and climate scalars: home_adj_xg = home_exp_goals * (1 + home_tactical_s) * (1 + home_climate_modifier).
Climate modifier per team is a piecewise function on origin temperature: <10C: -0.08, <=20C: 0, <=26C: 0.05, >26C: -0.10.
Match-level situational_modifier = match_tactical_r + venue_penalty, where match_tactical_r = AVG(home_tactical_s, away_tactical_s) and venue_penalty is from venue_tier.
Venue penalty: extreme: -0.20, high: -0.15, altitude: -0.15, moderate: -0.08, mild: 0.
adjusted_total_exp_goals = (home_adj_xg + away_adj_xg) * (1 + situational_modifier).
Three-layer multiplicative structure (input adjustment, per-team scalars, match-level scalar) ensures environmental effects scale proportionally with projected goal volume.
O/U line varies by match (typically 2.5 but sometimes 1.5, 3.5, 4.5) based on the Kalshi contract offered for that match.
P(under L) = sum of Poisson(k; adjusted_total) for k = 0 to floor(L). P(over L) = 1 - P(under L).
O/U market probabilities are normalized separately from moneyline using over_raw and under_raw.
O/U signal thresholds match moneyline thresholds.
Knockout-stage rows show #N/A in venue_tier and situational_modifier until the bracket resolves post-group-stage; this is expected, not a bug.
model_output is the clean final dashboard for moneyline decision-making.
model_output pulls from model_inputs_v02 for official moneyline signals.
model_output includes model probabilities, market probabilities, edges, best_value, best_edge, signal, review_flag, draw_play_filter, weak_schedule_match, and model_pick.
ou_model is the O/U output dashboard, separate from model_output.
ou_model includes adjusted_total_exp_goals, under_prob, over_prob, market_over, market_under, edges, ou_best_value, ou_best_edge, ou_signal, ou_review_flag.
Signal colors used for visual triage: STRONG PLAY, PLAY, WATCH, PASS, REVIEW.
Before kickoff, official model tabs are duplicated and pasted as values only.
Frozen tabs (dated): model_inputs_v02_FROZEN_<MMDD>, model_output_FROZEN_<MMDD>, daily_odds_FROZEN_<MMDD>, ou_model_FROZEN_<MMDD>.
Freezing preserves the exact pre-match model outputs and prevents accidental retroactive changes.
Frozen tabs should be created at T-1hr after final Kalshi prices are entered and before kickoff.
Frozen outputs protect against accidental retroactive formula changes or data updates contaminating the forward test.
live_results_tracker is the live performance ledger for the project.

live_results_tracker records: match_id, date, home_team, away_team, city, stage, model probs (frozen), market probs (frozen), model_pick, best_value, best_edge, signal, weak_schedule_match, stake, side_bet, entry_price, actual_outcome, model_pick_hit (auto), best_value_hit (auto), pnl, clv.
Moneyline performance tracks model_pick_hit and best_value_hit separately.
O/U performance tracks whether ou_best_value hit based on the relevant O/U line.
Primary validation method is live forward testing during the 2026 World Cup.
Before each match, final Kalshi prices entered, model_outputs checked, frozen outputs preserved before kickoff.
After each match, actual_outcome and ou_result recorded in live_results_tracker.
Forward testing avoids look-ahead bias and preserves real pre-match decision conditions.
Initial evaluation: model_pick accuracy, best_value hit rate, signal-tier performance, draw performance, weak-schedule bucket performance, O/U hit rate.
Calibration evaluated after meaningful sample by grouping predictions into probability buckets: 40-50%, 50-60%, 60-70%, 70-80%, 80%+.
Draw recommendations evaluated separately because draw probability is the most fragile part of the model.
REVIEW rows analyzed separately from official PLAY and STRONG PLAY rows.
CLV (closing line value) tracked for all bets placed; positive CLV indicates beating closing market price (pro-bettor metric).
v0.3 O/U evaluated side-by-side with archived v0.2 O/U for relative performance comparison.
Backtesting is a credibility supplement; official evaluation prioritizes live forward testing.
Initial backtest is a 2022 World Cup sanity check, not a fully optimized ML backtest.
First backtest tests whether higher model probabilities generally aligned with actual outcomes in 2022 WC.
Backtesting evaluates model_pick accuracy separately from best_value edge performance.
Historical market-edge backtesting requires reliable historical Kalshi-equivalent prices; without those, only prediction quality (not market mispricing) can be backtested.
v0.2 moneyline is a hand-weighted scorecard model, not a machine-learning model. Weights are educated initial values, not optimized.
v0.3 O/U situational factor weights (tactical, climate, venue) are also hand-set and uncalibrated; v0.2 O/U archived for side-by-side comparison.
Weights should not be aggressively re-tuned on individual match results.
Reliable calibration conclusions require 20+ matches.
xG availability varies by confederation; regional sample sizes and competition strength are partially normalized in O/U (via conf_scalar) but not in moneyline.
Goal differential is not fully opponent-adjusted; teams with weak qualifying schedules may look artificially strong.
Draw probabilities are heuristic; replacement with Poisson scoreline grid or calibrated draw classifier is a v1.1 candidate.
conf_scalar values, especially CONMEBOL at 0.88, are uncalibrated and should be revisited with forward-test data.
Kalshi prices move before kickoff; final signals must use the latest prices.
REVIEW rows are not final trading recommendations.
Knockout-stage venue and situational data populate only after group stage ends; pre-group-stage knockout O/U projections are not produced.
Logistic regression weight optimization on accumulated forward-test sample.
Draw probability replacement via Poisson scoreline grid or calibrated draw classifier.
v0.3 moneyline overlay promotion to production after situational factor calibration (with capped situational score).
conf_scalar values recalibrated using observed CLV by confederation after group stage.
Opponent-adjusted goal differential to address Norway-type schedule strength bias.
KO-stage O/U model recalibration added post-group-stage once bracket is known.
Public results dashboard with running calibration plots and weak-schedule-bucketed performance.
